spike_verdict: Carried by the evidence in substance (F06, F07, F08 confirm the death, mutilation, burial, and later restoration), but the page overstates causation: the source never says the inquest itself ordered the mutilation/burial, only that it happened after the inquest.

blocking.where: composition.json spike_statement; history.mdx 'What Happened to Babs'; showcase.json spike_explainer 'Erasure, not memorial'
blocking.claim: "his car Babs was mutilated on inquest orders" / "the wreck was buried in the dunes at Pendine on the inquest's instruction" / "on the inquest's instruction it was buried in the sand dunes"
blocking.problem: Overstated causation. The cited source (F07) says only that the mutilation and burial happened AFTER/FOLLOWING the inquest — it never states the inquest itself ordered or instructed these acts. 'On inquest orders' / 'on the inquest's instruction' asserts a specific official directive that the source does not establish.
blocking.evidence: Wikipedia, Babs (car) — verbatim: "Following the inquest into Thomas's death, Babs's seats were slashed, the glass in the dials smashed, and the car was buried in the sand dunes at Pendine." (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babs_(land_speed_record_car) — confirmed by direct re-fetch this session; no sentence anywhere in the article attributes the decision to the inquest.)
blocking.fix: Replace 'mutilated on inquest orders' with 'mutilated after the inquest into his death' in the spike_statement. Replace 'buried in the dunes at Pendine on the inquest's instruction' (history.mdx) and 'on the inquest's instruction it was buried in the sand dunes at Pendine' (showcase.json) with 'buried in the dunes at Pendine following the inquest' — dropping the implication that the inquest itself ordered it.

blocking.where: travel.mdx 'Driving on the Sand'; showcase.json honest_reckoning_note
blocking.claim: "Until 2005, any visitor could drive onto Pendine Sands. All vehicle access was then banned outright between 9 July 2004 and May 2010 on safety grounds..."
blocking.problem: Self-contradictory date claim: the passage asserts free driving continued until 2005, then in the very next sentence says the ban started 9 July 2004 — a date before 2005. Both cannot be true. This is an unreconciled collision between two of the sheet's own sources: Classic & Sports Car's framing ('until 2005, any visitor could drive on the beach') and Wikipedia's precise ban window (F14: '9 July 2004' to May 2010). showcase.json's intro_text compounds it, separately stating paid permission has been required 'since 2005.'
blocking.evidence: F33 (Classic & Sports Car, Oct 2024) quote: 'until 2005, any visitor could drive on the beach - and you still can if you're prepared to pay £2000 a day...' vs. F14 (Wikipedia) quote: 'between 9 july 2004 and may 2010 all vehicles were banned from using pendine because of safety concerns.' The fact sheet's own conflicts list flags a related but distinct 2004-vs-2005 discrepancy between two Wikipedia articles; this page-level collision (free-until-2005 stated adjacent to a ban-from-2004) is a further, uncaught version of the same unresolved conflict.
blocking.fix: Delete the standalone claim 'Until 2005, any visitor could drive onto Pendine Sands' from travel.mdx and the parallel sentence in showcase.json's honest_reckoning_note. Keep only the precisely-dated claim: 'All vehicle access was banned outright between 9 July 2004 and May 2010 on safety grounds; cars have been allowed back since, now at £2,000/day with prior permission.' In showcase.json intro_text, change '...has required paid, pre-arranged permission from Carmarthenshire's local authorities since 2005' to '...has required paid, pre-arranged permission from Carmarthenshire's local authorities since cars were allowed back in 2010' to remove the conflicting year.

advisory.where: composition.json subtitle; history.mdx 'One further attempt was planned...'
advisory.claim: "five land-speed record attempts were made between 1924 and 1927"
advisory.problem: The fifth 'attempt' (Foresti, Nov 1927) never actually happened as a record attempt — per F09 and the page's own text, Foresti crashed his car Djelmo 'during a test run,' destroying it before any record attempt could be made. A strict count is four actual attempts (1924, 1926, Feb 1927, fatal March 1927) plus one planned attempt aborted by a pre-run crash.
advisory.evidence: F09 quote: 'foresti crashed during a test run on 26 november 1927, totally destroying the car' — the crash occurred in testing, not in the record attempt itself.
advisory.fix: Optional: soften subtitle to 'five bids for the land-speed record' or 'the site of five land-speed record efforts' to cover the aborted Foresti case without asserting all five runs were actually made. Not required if 'attempt' is read loosely enough to include a fatal preparatory crash.

advisory.where: history.mdx 'The Record Didn't End in 1927 — It Moved On'
advisory.claim: "On 21 July 2015, the 90th anniversary of Campbell's first Pendine record, Wales returned to drive the fully restored original Blue Bird"
advisory.problem: Arithmetic: Campbell's first Pendine record was 25 Sept 1924; 2015 minus 1924 is 91, not 90. This mismatch is inherited verbatim from the cited Wikipedia source (F19), not introduced by the page.
advisory.evidence: F19 quote: 'on 21 july 2015, at pendine beach, the 90th anniversary of sir malcolm campbell's first world land speed record ... was recreated...' — the source itself appears to miscount by a year.
advisory.fix: No page-level fix needed; the page faithfully repeats a source-level inconsistency. Optional: drop the '90th anniversary' framing and just state the date, to sidestep the source's arithmetic.
